name: MonarchJsonViewer
title: JSONViewer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn over a flattened model of the open part of the tree; MonarchTextField for search, MonarchButton for Collapse all, MonarchCopyButton for Copy path and Copy value
summary: A collapsible, searchable tree for a JSON document, with copy path and copy value for the selected node, that stays fast on large payloads.
whenToUse: In developer and support tools, to inspect webhook payloads, API responses, event data or settings stored as JSON.
whenNotToUse: For a short JSON snippet the user reads or copies whole, use MonarchCodeBlock; for a hierarchy of records that are not JSON, use MonarchTreeView; for a few labelled values, MonarchDescriptionList.
api: @Composable fun MonarchJsonViewer(value: MonarchJsonValue, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, expandDepth: Int = 1, maxChildren: Int = 100, maxStringLength: Int = 500, searchable: Boolean = true, maxMatches: Int = 500, copyable: Boolean = true, rootPath: String = "$", searchIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, clearIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchJsonViewerLabels = MonarchJsonViewerLabels(), onSelect: ((path: String, value: MonarchJsonValue) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)

sealed interface MonarchJsonValue { data class Object(members: List<Pair<String, MonarchJsonValue>>); data class Array(items: List<MonarchJsonValue>); data class String(value: String); data class Number(text: String); data class Bool(value: Boolean); data object Null; companion object { fun parse(text: String): MonarchJsonValue; fun from(value: Any?): MonarchJsonValue } }

class MonarchJsonViewerLabels(label: String? = null, search: String? = null, searchPrompt: String? = null, clearSearch: String? = null, matches: ((count: Int, capped: Boolean) -> String)? = null, collapseAll: String? = null, copyPath: String? = null, copyValue: String? = null, selectedPath: String? = null, keys: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, items: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showMore: ((next: Int, remaining: Int) -> String)? = null, truncated: ((length: Int) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The document. Build it with MonarchJsonValue.parse, which keeps the order of object keys and the exact text of numbers, with MonarchJsonValue.from for Kotlin maps and lists, or with the cases.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end, such as a MonarchIcon of size Sm with mirrorInRtl = true. It turns a quarter turn while its container is open. Required, as in MonarchTreeView, because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the viewer. The rows scroll inside it: give it a bounded height, or let it fill a screen or pane.

options.name: expandDepth
options.description: Levels open at first: 1 shows the root's children, 0 only the root.

options.name: maxChildren
options.description: Children shown per object or array before a "Show more" row; each Show more adds this many. At least 1.

options.name: maxStringLength
options.description: Strings longer than this are cut in the tree with "… (n characters)". Copy value always copies the whole string.

options.name: searchable
options.description: Shows the search field and the match count.

options.name: maxMatches
options.description: The search stops after this many matches and the count shows "500+ matches".

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows the footer with the selected path, Copy path and Copy value.

options.name: rootPath
options.description: The first part of shown and copied paths: $ gives $.users[0].name, an empty string gives users[0].name.

options.name: searchIcon
options.description: An icon at the start of the search field.

options.name: clearIcon
options.description: The icon of a button that clears the search, shown while there is a query. Without it the search is cleared by deleting the text or with Collapse all.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the rows.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the tree name, the search field, the match count, Collapse all, the copy buttons, the selected path, the summaries, Show more, the cut string suffix and the spoken open state.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the formatted path and the value when the user selects another node (a tap, Show more or Collapse all).

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied text after the path or the value is copied.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: A closed object or array shows the chevron pointing to the end and its summary: { } 3 keys or [ ] 2 items.

states.name: expanded
states.description: An open container shows the chevron turned a quarter and its children, indented one level.

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected row has the muted fill and the selected state; the footer shows its path. The root is selected at first.

states.name: searching
states.description: Containers that hold a match open, matched text is highlighted and bold, and the toolbar shows the match count.

states.name: show more
states.description: A container with more children than maxChildren ends with a link-coloured "Show 100 more (250 hidden)" row. Search reveals hidden children that match.

states.name: collapsed all
states.description: Collapse all clears the search, closes every container below the root and selects the root.

appearance: The viewer is a surface-coloured box with a subtle border and 12dp corners, with subtle lines between the toolbar, the rows and the footer. Rows are code text: object keys in the strong info color, array indexes and punctuation muted, strings in the strong success color, numbers in the strong accent color, booleans and null in the strong warning color. The selected row has the muted background; matches have the subtle warning background and are bold. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web takes any JavaScript value and shows circular references, undefined and Dates; on Android, as on iOS, the input is MonarchJsonValue, which cannot be circular, parsed by a small parser that keeps key order and number text (org.json does not promise either). The web's tree keyboard pattern (arrows, Home, End, *) is replaced by touch: tapping a row selects it and opens or closes it, and TalkBack moves row by row. The plan's dependency tree-view is not used directly: MonarchTreeView takes labels as plain strings and keeps the expanded set in the app, while the viewer needs coloured, highlighted key and value text and its own flattened, batched model; the chevron convention (expandIcon pointing to the end, a quarter turn when open) is the same. Search is a MonarchTextField rather than MonarchSearchBar, which expands into a search view of its own. Monarch bundles no icons, so expandIcon is required and searchIcon and clearIcon are optional. onCopy receives the text only; the web also passes whether it was the path or the value. The toolbar has no slot for extra actions. iOS uses the same name; Android adds expandIcon, searchIcon, clearIcon and state, and uses Kotlin-style booleans (searchable, copyable) and PascalCase value cases.
accessibility: Each row is a button read as "key: value", such as "amount: 4200" or "lines: [ ] 2 items".
Containers have Expanded or Collapsed as their state description; the chevron is decorative.
The selected row has the selected state, and the footer path is read as "Selected, <path>".
Matches are bold as well as highlighted, so they are not shown by color alone.
The match count is a polite live region, so a new count is announced while searching.
Rows, Show more and the copy buttons are at least 48dp tall.
Copy path and Copy value are MonarchCopyButton, which says "Copied to clipboard" after a copy.
edgeCases: Only open containers are walked, so a closed 10 MB document costs one row; search walks the whole document once per query and stops at maxMatches.
Long keys and values wrap; very long strings are cut at maxStringLength in the tree only.
A repeated key in parsed text keeps its first position and its last value, as JSON.parse does. Repeated keys built by hand are not merged; avoid them, because rows are identified by path.
Numbers keep the text they were written with (1.50, 12345678901234567890).
A primitive root is one row; an empty object or array cannot open.
MonarchJsonValue.parse rejects nesting deeper than 100 levels with MonarchJsonParseException, which also bounds the recursion of search, flattening and copying.
The open state, limits and selection reset when the value changes; the query is kept across configuration changes.
